findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a platform-portable signing shim strategy for AC1 (e.g., a Python-executable shim script invoked via `gpg.program = python -c ...`, or a `.bat` fallback on Windows) so the fixture produces genuinely signed commits and AC1 is non-vacuous across all supported platforms.
evidence: Plan states: 'The signing is load-bearing: with --format=%H over *unsigned* commits the setting emits no extra lines, so an unsigned fixture makes this vacuously green'
Plan states: 'a `gpg.program` / `gpg.format` shim suffices' — implicitly assumes a shim is executable by git on all platforms

On Windows (a supported platform in the matrix), a POSIX shell-script shim assigned to gpg.program is not directly executable without WSL/Git Bash; git commit -S would fail or fall back, yielding unsigned commits
The plan does not specify a platform-portable shim strategy (e.g., a Python script shim or a .bat wrapper)
findings.finding: AC1 specifies a signed-commit fixture using 'a gpg.program / gpg.format shim' but does not address Windows, where a shell-script shim is not directly executable. If the shim silently fails on Windows, git produces unsigned commits, and — as the plan itself warns — 'an unsigned fixture makes this vacuously green', meaning the most load-bearing AC proves nothing on that platform.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, first bullet: "a `gpg.program` / `gpg.format` shim suffices"
scenarios: Windows platform, developer workstation or CI: the shell-script gpg.program shim is not executable; git commit -S either errors or skips signing; the fixture contains unsigned commits; AC1 passes vacuously, providing no coverage of the actual showSignature bug on Windows
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the shell-script shim assumption with a Python-based shim: set `gpg.program` to a small Python one-liner or a `sys.executable`-invoked helper that writes a minimal fake PGP signature to stdout. Python is guaranteed available in the rebar test environment on all platforms, making the shim portable without WSL or Git Bash.

evidence: Plan quote: 'an unsigned fixture makes this vacuously green'
The fix under test is `lines[-1]` returning a non-SHA when GPG lines are interleaved; if no GPG lines are interleaved, the test never exercises the defect path

Plan says 'a gpg.program / gpg.format shim suffices' but does not specify the shim must emit GPG-style interleaved lines into git log stdout, nor that the test should verify raw log output contains non-hex lines before asserting the SHA result
findings.finding: AC 1 is explicitly flagged by the plan itself as 'vacuously green' when unsigned commits are used, yet the plan does not prescribe a concrete guard that forces the fixture to actually emit interleaved GPG lines into git-log stdout. A test author who builds the fixture with unsigned commits will see AC 1 pass even without the fix, meaning the live latent bug (non-SHA lines[-1] under log.showSignature=true) remains undetected.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC 1 (Tier: unit, signed-commit fixture)
scenarios: Test author creates fixture repo with unsigned commits → AC 1 is green without the fix → PR merges → bug persists on hosts with log.showSignature=true and real signed commits
Shim is wired to sign silently (no stdout interleave) → same false-green outcome
